name: lazy-resume-on-attach
description: Restored panes replay as today, but the resume hook is held behind an in-pane confirmation prompt instead of firing at boot — with a preference for eager or lazy resumption.

bank.summary: Derive cmd/state_test.go's hand-written hidden-state-child name lists from stateChildCommands rather than restating them.
bank.failure: A new hidden state subcommand is added to the compile-checked stateChildCommands and silently escapes the two enumerations that have no catch-all, so the completions-leak guard and the argv-resolution guard stop covering the newest verbs. It ships green and is noticed either by a user tab-completing an internal verb or by a restored pane whose chain exec fails to resolve — which closes the pane. This task already hit it (resume-draw missing from both), and tasks 4.2 and 4.4 add two more chain subcommands that will hit it again.
bank.detail: names at cmd/state_test.go:261 (TestStateChildrenRemainInvocableByArgv) and hidden at cmd/state_test.go:287 (TestStateHiddenSubcommandsAbsentFromShellCompletions) are complete-set lists with no catch-all; hidden at :78 is the same list but backed by an unexpected-command catch-all, and :103 is deliberately partial. Replace the first two with a loop over stateChildCommands reading c.Name().

bank.summary: Fold the resume-chain commands' flag reset into resetRootCmd rather than leaving a second, locally-called reset helper.
bank.failure: A cmd test that drives a resume-chain subcommand through resetRootCmd() + Execute inherits flag values left Changed on the shared command instance by an earlier Execute, so its assertion passes while checking nothing. Demonstrated, not hypothetical — the executor hit it in this task (the --command refusal subtest passed vacuously when run after its sibling) and patched it with a helper local to one test file. Tasks 4.2 and 4.4 register resume-wait and resume-recover with the same flag set and the same shared-instance hazard, and whoever writes them has no signal the reset exists or must be called. It ships green; the defect it hides surfaces as a resume-chain command parsing a stale payload in a restored pane.
bank.detail: resetRootCmd (cmd/root_test.go:20-95) is the canonical per-command flag reset and already carries stateHydrateCmd's three flags at :90-95. resetResumeDrawFlags (cmd/state_resume_draw_test.go:348) is a second home for that same responsibility, reachable only from its own file. A VisitAll-over-stateChildCommands loop inside resetRootCmd would cover the hydrate flags, resume-draw, and the two chain commands still to land, in one edit. Pairs naturally with the already-banked stateChildCommands derivation for cmd/state_test.go.

bank.summary: The resume chain's hand-off block (resolve exe → compose argv → exec INFO → ExecSelf) is now authored twice and Phase 4/5 will add three more copies.
bank.failure: The "exec INFO is the statement immediately before the exec" rule is enforced by nothing — every test fakes ExecSelf, so a later site that emits the marker after the exec, or omits it, fails no test and produces no symptom until an operator reconstructs why a pane fell through to a shell and finds the chain's last image unrecorded in portal.log. The same consolidation fixes the doubled prefix the empty-path branch produces today ("resolve portal executable: resolve portal executable: empty path"), since both call sites wrap an error that already carries that prefix.
bank.detail: cmd/state_resume_draw.go:56-68 and cmd/state_resume_wait.go:96-109 are the two copies; the natural home for one resumeHandOff(logger, execSelf, subcommand, payload) is cmd/state_resume_chain.go, beside resumeChainArgv/resumeChainExe, where the empty-path error string (state_resume_chain.go:81) can lose its duplicate prefix at the same time. Worth taking at the phase boundary, once 4.3, 4.4 and Phase 5 have added their sites and the shape has stopped moving.

bank.summary: The store-lookup degradation rule is now written twice, once per resume path.
bank.failure: The eager path (execShellOrHookAndExit) and the lazy path (resumeCommandAtAnswer) each decide independently that a miss, an empty command or a read error means a bare shell, and each emits its own hook lookup DEBUG / lookup on-resume hook failed WARN. A later change to one — a new result value, a mode check, a different fallback — compiles and leaves both suites green, so a pane resumed from the panel behaves differently from the same pane resumed at hydrate, and the user sees it only as "my hook ran on reboot but not when I pressed Enter".
bank.detail: cmd/state_hydrate.go:174-198 (execShellOrHookAndExit) and cmd/state_resume_wait.go:122-139 (resumeCommandAtAnswer) encode the same three-branch rule over two different config types; a shared "logger + hook key" shape would give it one home. Phase 5's discard path reads the same store again and may add a third site.

bank.summary: The line that lifts the freeze has no end-to-end verification, and cannot get one until the arming side exists.
bank.failure: state.UnsetResumePendingMarker(tmux.DefaultClient(), tmux.PaneIDTarget(pane)) is exercised by nothing. internal/state pins the marker function against a mock writer and internal/tmux pins the option write, but the composition is untested, and its two silent mis-wirings both compile: cfg.PaneKey in place of cfg.Pane (plain strings on the same payload, registered as adjacent flags on the same command), or tmux.PaneTarget in place of tmux.PaneIDTarget (both return tmux.Target). Either yields a target no pane answers to — Enter then loops the panel forever with a tmux error on its report row — or, worse, a target that does answer, clearing another pane's marker while this pane is handed over still frozen. That last state is precisely what §7.2 exists to prevent: the pane's saved scrollback frozen for the rest of its life, every reboot restoring the transcript it held when it paused, with no sweep that reaches a pane option and no waiter left to report it. The user notices weeks later, as a session that restores stale content.
bank.detail: cmd/state_resume_wait.go:223-225 (the ClearMarker closure). No unit-lane route exists because the closure hardcodes tmux.DefaultClient(); no integration route exists because nothing in production sets the marker yet (state.SetResumePendingMarker has no production caller). Once arming lands, one integration test over a tmuxtest socket closes it for both answer paths at once — mark via Socket.MarkResumePending, answer the wait, assert Socket.ReadResumePending reads empty — since Phase 5's discard clears the same marker through the same seam.

bank.summary: Sharpening of the store-degradation entry: the two sites have ALREADY diverged on a Found result carrying an empty command.
bank.failure: execShellOrHookAndExit treats Found with an empty command as a hit and would exec sh -c "; exec $SHELL", while resumeCommandAtAnswer treats it as a miss. The divergence is currently harmless only because LookupOnResume never produces that state (internal/hooks/lookup.go:36-39 degrades a stored value carrying no command to the zero result) — which is evidence for consolidating the rule rather than against it. A change to that degradation makes the two paths disagree immediately.
bank.detail: Attaches to the executor-banked entry naming cmd/state_hydrate.go:174-198 and cmd/state_resume_wait.go:122-139. Consequence to note when folding: the "empty command" acceptance criterion of task 4-3 is satisfiable only through a seam-level fake, since that branch is unreachable via the production lookup.

bank.summary: ResolveHookKey and the new ReadPaneOption each carry their own copy of the measured probe-then-read discrimination, in the same package.
bank.failure: The two copies encode one tmux fact (a format read answers a gone pane with exit 0 and an empty string, so the option-less show-options probe is what separates "gone" from "unset"). If someone simplifies either copy to a lone display-message — it looks redundant and every test that only uses live panes stays green — a gone pane starts reading as a live pane carrying no option. On ResolveHookKey's path that turns portal hook set against a vanished pane from a clean failure into a mint-stamp-write against nothing, which is the junk-key class of bug the probe was added to close; on ReadPaneOption's path a gone pane reads as "answered" and the chain tail silently declines to recover it. Noticed only as a stray hooks.json entry or a pane that closed, long after the edit.
bank.detail: ResolveHookKey (internal/tmux/tmux.go:250-263) could be expressed as ReadPaneOption(paneID, state.PortalPaneIDOption) — identical two-read sequence, differing only in the error wording and in passing the format positionally rather than under -F (behaviourally the same to tmux). Consolidating leaves one declaration of the rule and one place the probe can be wrongly removed from.

bank.summary: The argv→shell-command-string renderer is now declared twice, in two packages, with identical bodies.
bank.failure: internal/shellquote is the tree's single declaration of the POSIX quoting rule because naive composition corrupts a user-authored command; the joining half of that rule is now declared separately in cmd.shellWords and internal/spawn.renderCommandString, with no exported route to it. The next site that has to render an argv into a shell word list — phase 5's redraw/discard chain is the near-term candidate — has no obvious helper to reach for and hand-rolls a third copy, or concatenates. Noticed by a user whose resume command holds a space, a quote or a $ reaching the panel's draw as several arguments, or truncated.
bank.detail: cmd/state_resume_chain.go:75-83 and internal/spawn/recipe.go:70-76 are byte-identical modulo variable names (make([]string, len(argv)) → shellquote.Single per element → strings.Join(…, " ")). The consolidation is an exported joiner on internal/shellquote (which both already import) with both call sites routed through it; it reaches internal/spawn, so it is outside task 4-5's scope.

bank.summary: Two hydrate test names now state the inverse of the ordering this phase established; they are the last statement of the superseded ordering left in the repo.
bank.failure: TestHydrate_SignalArrived_LookupHappensAfterSleepAndMarkerUnset and TestHydrate_FileMissing_LookupHappensAfterMarkerUnset name an ordering that no longer holds — the lookup now happens at the top of runHydrate, before both clears. The executor corrected the comments inside both bodies to say "hand-off", so each test now carries a name and a comment that contradict each other. A later reader trusting the name re-derives the superseded ordering, and the bodies do still pin a real property, so nothing goes red to correct them.
bank.detail: cmd/state_hydrate_test.go:1667 and :1727. The whole remedy is renaming both to name the hand-off rather than the lookup. Raised by the 4-5 reviewer as an observation rather than a finding, since finding-floor.md excludes test-file naming; recorded here so the boundary pass can confirm or drop it against the final state.
